newsitem.title: UK: UK's C5 says on course for five pct audience share.
newsitem.headline: UK's C5 says on course for five pct audience share.

text.p: Britain's Channel 5, launched two months ago, is on course to meet its target of a five percent TV audience share by the end of the year, chief executive David Elstein said on Wednesday.
"Before the end of the year we expect to be in more than 70 percent of UK homes and to achieve five percent weekly shares," Elstein said in a statement.
"Coverage will increase, reach will grow and our audience share will climb in line with these developments. As a business, 5 is looking stronger by the day," he added.
Channel 5, in which UK media companies United News & Media Plc and Pearson Plc are big shareholders, has been criticised in the press over the quality of programmes and reception problems.

But the national terrestrial channel, launched on March 30, attracted five million viewers -- by far its best audience to date -- for Saturday's live coverage of the Poland-England World Cup soccer match.
Elstein called the match a "watershed" and the channel hopes the success will have raised its profile and persuaded more viewers to adjust their sets to receive its signal.
Channel 5 said nearly 60 percent of UK households had now sampled it. It estimated that a further 5-10 percent of homes may be able to receive the channel.

Its reach should be boosted later in the year when nine new transmitters kick in but it will remain unavailable in some areas of Britain. Cable and satellite coverage has been secured in a bid to fill in the gaps.

Channel 5 said its average weekly viewing share of all homes was 2.7 percent. It said it was succeeding in its drive to win younger viewers, more than a third of its audience falling into the 16-34 bracket.

Channel 5, in which U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus and European broadcast group CLT are the other shareholders, is operating on a modest core programming budget of 110 million pounds ($180 million).
However, it recently splashed out some 90 million pounds to win a film deal with Warner Brothers, beating off competition from the ITV commercial network.
It has also signed a deal to broadcast Chelsea's home soccer matches in next season's European Cup Winners' Cup.
